release_notes.headline: The foundation for reproducible NeoBSD releases
release_notes.summary: NeoBSD 26.0 establishes the core: a clear release architecture with targets, profile-driven builds, and ordered patch series. The result is predictable, reproducible releases from source state to final artifact.
highlights: Introduced the core model for targets and release intent
Profile-based build configuration as a default baseline
Reliable orchestration for preparation, patching, build, and publishing

release_notes.headline: More mount flexibility, no compromise on safety
release_notes.summary: With 26.1, cell mounts become more flexible: optional host-path nullfs mounts are now possible while staying explicitly opt-in by design. The neobsd-11 target patch state was also cleanly integrated.
highlights: Optional host-path mounts for cells
Secure defaults remain intact (explicit opt-in)
Updated patch state for neobsd-11

release_notes.headline: Faster path from host artifacts to running cells
release_notes.summary: 26.2 modernizes artifact workflows with declarative COPY and UNTAR steps. It also adds optional profile-based build branding, improving day-to-day usability and giving releases a clearer identity.
highlights: New COPY and UNTAR directives
Automatic reconciliation when source artifacts change
Optional profile-driven branding for build.sh

release_notes.headline: A clean home for vendor software in every cell
release_notes.summary: With 26.3, each cell gets a writable /opt overlay path. That gives third-party software outside pkg/pkgsrc a consistent, well-structured place in the system layout.
highlights: Writable per-cell /opt via overlay
Cleaner structure for vendor deployments
Consistent behavior with existing overlay mechanics

release_notes.headline: Declarative run-as for safer, deterministic services
release_notes.summary: 26.4 takes supervised services to the next level: run-as is now declarative, identities are resolved cleanly, and supervision follows a fail-closed model. That means stronger security and more predictable runtime behavior.
highlights: Declarative run-as for supervised services
Reliable runtime UID/GID/group resolution
Least-privilege execution with deterministic startup flow

release_notes.headline: File ownership now follows runtime identity automatically
release_notes.summary: With 26.5, apply plans become even more practical: ownership placeholders tie file permissions directly to service runtime identities. This reduces operational friction and prevents permission drift.
highlights: owner=@run_uid and group=@run_gid in apply plans
Support across DIR, COPY, and FILE_BEGIN
Run identity now influences apply reconciliation

release_notes.headline: Resolve run-as identities directly inside the cell
release_notes.summary: 26.6 makes identity mapping feel natural: run-as can be defined in cell context using cell:user[:group]. This simplifies configuration, especially in larger multi-cell environments.
highlights: In-cell identity resolution for run-as
Support for cell:user[:group] syntax
Consistent behavior across CLI, docs, and man pages

release_notes.headline: Cells v3 has arrived: a new control plane for the next stage
release_notes.summary: 26.7 is a major leap forward: with cellman/libcellman and a Lua DSL, the third generation of cell control plane is now integrated. The result is a clearer operations model with stronger structure, safety, and scalability.
highlights: Introduced the v3 control plane (cellman/libcellman)
Declarative Lua models for desired system state
Stronger safety defaults and runtime guards
Integrated consolidated third-generation cells into NeoBSD

release_notes.headline: Bugfix: Restored missing cellman examples
release_notes.summary: NeoBSD 26.8 addresses an oversight in 26.7 where the cellman examples were unintentionally omitted. This release restores the complete set of examples, ensuring that the new v3 control plane can be explored and adopted with proper guidance.
highlights: Restored missing cellman example configurations
Improved out-of-the-box usability of the v3 control plane
No functional changes to core system behavior

release_notes.headline: Re-based on NetBSD 11.0_RC4
release_notes.summary: NeoBSD 26.9 rebases the system on top of NetBSD 11.0_RC4 to align with the newer upstream foundation and keep target behavior current.
highlights: Re-based NeoBSD on NetBSD 11.0_RC4
Aligned base system with current upstream release candidate
Prepared the groundwork for follow-up compatibility updates

release_notes.headline: Hardened secmodel_cell with transactional lifecycle and stronger ABI defenses
release_notes.summary: NeoBSD 26.10 significantly strengthens secmodel_cell internals. Cell create, enter, and destroy paths now use explicit lifecycle states, hold-based quiescence checks, and strict lock-order discipline to close race windows under concurrent churn. Sysctl control paths enforce bounded NUL-terminated text input and sequence-coherent list snapshots, while policy denies now expose atomic counters and per-scope rate-limited audit telemetry.
highlights: Introduced explicit lifecycle-state and hold-counted transactions so destroy and enter cannot race into inconsistent membership state
Hardened management input handling with bounded NUL checks, control-character rejection, and stricter fixed-size payload validation
Made list/stat exports snapshot-coherent across lock drop/reacquire boundaries with sequence validation and overflow-aware sizing
Added atomic deny counters and per-scope rate-limited audit logging for process, system, and network policy rejects
Improved module lifecycle hygiene with clean listener-start failure unwinds and consistent teardown of runtime resources
